title: Microsoft Purview Data Governance — Data Map, Scanning & Unified Catalog
author_notes: Effort tier: T5 (enterprise Microsoft Purview implementation).

Microsoft Purview portal / Security & Compliance PowerShell / Graph authored at exact detail from Microsoft public docs; Purview features are heavily licensing-/plan-dependent (E5 / E5 Compliance; some preview) and the portal is evolving — availability + paths cited or flagged 'verify your licensing/tenant', never invented. Regulatory/records/legal determinations (retention schedules, file plans, legal holds, insider-risk case actions) deferred to compliance/records/privacy/legal — solutions give the technical method + evidence, not the determination; policies piloted in simulation/test before enforcement. Automation is PowerShell (S&C PowerShell / Graph); no secrets in code. No client names.
hook: Map, classify, and govern the data estate — not just M365
problem: Beyond M365, your data lives in databases, data lakes, and clouds — ungoverned and unclassified. This flagship solution implements Microsoft Purview Data Governance: build the Data Map (register sources across Azure, multicloud, and on-prem), run scanning + classification, curate the Unified Catalog (data products, glossary, ownership), establish data-quality and governance domains, and wire lineage — so the whole data estate is discoverable, classified, and governed, not just Microsoft 365.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the Data Map, scanning + classification, the Unified Catalog (data products, glossary, domains, ownership), lineage, and how it complements M365 Purview.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (Purview Data Governance licensing/setup, roles/domains, source credentials + network, data owners).

Implementation Guide — stand up the account/domains + roles, register + scan sources, curate the catalog (glossary, classifications, data products, ownership), wire lineage + data quality, and expand across the estate — pilot-first, each domain/source named.

5 PowerShell scripts — Discovery, Configuration/Remediation, Validation, Reporting, and a scope/health helper — authentic Security & Compliance PowerShell / Graph automation (read-only or -WhatIf by default; no credentials in code).
Validation gates (sources scanned + classified, catalog curated, ownership assigned) plus Best Practices for a governed, discoverable data estate.
short: Implement Purview Data Governance — the Data Map, scanning + classification, the Unified Catalog (glossary, data products, domains, ownership), and lineage — so the whole data estate (not just M365) is discoverable, classified, and governed. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
